Primary_Symptoms: Unilateral throbbing or pulsating headache preceded by visual aura (flashing lights, zigzag lines, blind spots) or sensory paresthesias
Secondary_Symptoms: Photophobia; Phonophobia; Nausea; Vomiting; Transient numbness/tingling in hand or face
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Sirdard se pehle aakhon ke aage roshni ke dhabbe, chamak, ya sunn-pan aata hai?; 2. Sirdard sar ke ek hi taraf hota hai?; 3. Sirdard mahine me kitni baar hota hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Naproxen (Acute attack) / Sumatriptan (Rx under doctor)
Dosage_Frequency: TDS SOS (Paracetamol) / BD SOS (Naproxen) / Single dose at onset (Sumatriptan)
Supportive_Medicines: Domperidone 10 mg (for nausea); Propranolol / Amitriptyline (for prophylaxis if >2-4 attacks/month under neurologist)
Max_Safe_Limit_24h: 3250 mg Paracetamol / 1000 mg Naproxen / 100 mg Sumatriptan
Precautions_Contraindications: Simple analgesics (Paracetamol/Naproxen) first-line for acute attacks. Triptans are Rx only; contraindicated in ischemic heart disease, uncontrolled hypertension, history of stroke/TIA, and peripheral vascular disease. Avoid simple or combination analgesic use on more than 10-15 days per month to prevent Medication Overuse Headache. Ergotamine is Rx only and strictly contraindicated in pregnancy. Never stop or change preventive medication doses on your own
Home_Care_Advice: Rest in a quiet, dark, sound-proof room during an attack; Apply cold ice compress to forehead or temples; Maintain a consistent sleep schedule and hydration; Identify and avoid personal triggers (bright lights, missed meals, specific foods, stress)
Lab_Investigations: Clinical evaluation; MRI Brain (if atypical aura, persistent focal neurological deficits, or first episode after age 50)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Sudden worst headache of life ('Thunderclap'); Aura symptoms lasting >60 minutes; Persistent weakness or speech difficulty after headache resolves; Fever with stiff neck

Primary_Symptoms: Headache occurring on 15 or more days per month for >3 months, with at least 8 days per month meeting criteria for migraine headache
Secondary_Symptoms: Moderate to severe throbbing pain; Photophobia; Phonophobia; Nausea; Scalp allodynia; Daily functional impairment
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Mahine me 15 din se zyada sirdard rehta hai?; 2. Painkillers kitne din lete hain?; 3. Sirdard ke sath ulti ya roshni se takleef hoti hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - neurologist supervision required (Propranolol / Amitriptyline / Topiramate / Flunarizine / Botulinum Toxin)
Duration_Days: Rx - neurologist supervision required (3 to 6 months continuous prophylaxis)
Supportive_Medicines: Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Acute attack rescue medication (Sumatriptan SOS under strict limit)
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - neurologist supervision required. Never stop or change preventive doses on your own; sudden withdrawal can trigger severe rebound status migrainosus. Beta-blockers (Propranolol) contraindicated in asthma, sinus bradycardia, and heart block. Topiramate contraindicated in pregnancy (teratogenic) and acute glaucoma. Triptans contraindicated in coronary artery disease and uncontrolled HTN. Limit acute analgesic intake to <10 days/month to avoid Medication Overuse Headache
Home_Care_Advice: Maintain a strict daily headache diary tracking frequency, intensity, and medication use; Practice regular sleep-wake hygiene; Manage stress with relaxation techniques; Avoid acute painkiller overuse
Lab_Investigations: MRI Brain (rule out secondary structural causes); Complete Blood Count; Thyroid Profile (TSH)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Sudden explosive onset of severe unremitting headache; New neurological deficits (facial droop, arm weakness); Fever with neck stiffness; Progressive headache in cancer history

Common_Names_Hindi: Dawai ke zyada use se sirdard; Rebound Headache
Primary_Symptoms: Daily or near-daily headache present upon awakening, caused by regular overuse of acute headache medications for >3 months
Secondary_Symptoms: Dull, diffuse, pressing or migraine-like headache; Irritability; Nausea; Sleep disturbance; Dependence on daily painkillers
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Aap mahine me 10-15 din se zyada painkillers (Paracetamol/NSAIDs/Triptans) lete hain?; 2. Dawai ka asar khatam hote hi sirdard fir shuru ho jata hai?; 3. Subah uthte hi sirdard rehta hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Abrupt Discontinuation / Structured Taper of Overused Medication under Doctor + Prophylaxis
Supportive_Medicines: Antiemetics (Metoclopramide SOS during withdrawal phase); Non-pharmacological bridge therapy; Hydration
Precautions_Contraindications: Never stop or change medications on your own without medical guidance. Taper or abruptly stop the overused acute analgesic strictly under doctor supervision. Expect withdrawal rebound headache lasting 2-10 days after stopping overused pain medicine. Prevent re-starting frequent acute analgesics; limit all acute pain medicine to <8-10 days per month. Avoid combination analgesics containing caffeine or opioids
Home_Care_Advice: Understand that overused pain medicine is the cause, not the solution, for the daily headache; Drink plenty of fluids (2-3 liters daily); Rest during the initial withdrawal phase; Use non-drug relief (ice packs, dark room, gentle neck stretching)
Lab_Investigations: Clinical evaluation; MRI Brain (rule out underlying structural intracranial pathology)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Sudden severe 'thunderclap' headache; Persistent vomiting with dehydration; Confusion, seizures, or focal neurological deficits

Common_Names_Hindi: Trigeminal Neuralgia; Chehre ki nass ka tez dard
Primary_Symptoms: Sudden, severe, electric shock-like, stabbing paroxysmal facial pain along V1, V2, or V3 distribution of trigeminal nerve (usually unilateral)
Secondary_Symptoms: Pain triggered by light touch, chewing, washing face, brushing teeth, smiling, or cold wind; Pain-free refractory periods between spasms
Typical_Duration: Seconds to 2 minutes per spasm (recurrent episodes over weeks/months)
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Chehre par (gaal, jabde, ya aakh ke paas) achanak bijli ke jhatke jaisa tez stabbing dard hota hai?; 2. Khana chabane, brush karne, ya chehre ko choone par dard shuru hota hai?; 3. Dard kitni der rehta hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Carbamazepine OR Oxcarbazepine
Dosage_Frequency: BD initial, titrated slowly up to TDS by doctor
Supportive_Medicines: Pregabalin 75 mg OD at bedtime; Baclofen 10 mg BD (under specialist supervision)
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - neurologist supervision required. Carbamazepine is an antiepileptic drug; NEVER STOP OR CHANGE DOSE ON YOUR OWN (risk of severe rebound pain and seizures). HLA-B*1502 genetic testing recommended prior to starting carbamazepine in patients of Asian/Indian origin due to risk of fatal Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) / Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN). Monitor Complete Blood Count (risk of aplastic anemia/leukopenia) and Serum Sodium (risk of hyponatremia). Causes drowsiness, dizziness, and ataxia
Home_Care_Advice: Avoid known facial trigger zones during acute flares; Wash face with lukewarm water using soft gentle dabs; Eat soft foods and chew on unaffected side; Avoid cold wind drafts directly on face
Lab_Investigations: MRI Brain with thin-slice trigeminal nerve sequences (3D CISS/FIESTA - rules out neurovascular compression or Multiple Sclerosis); Complete Blood Count; Serum Electrolytes (Sodium); HLA-B*1502 screening
Emergency_Red_Flags: Severe generalized skin rash, fever, or mucosal ulcers (SJS/TEN reaction - STOP DRUG IMMEDIATELY AND GO TO ER); Progressive facial numbness or motor weakness; Unremitting agony preventing hydration

Common_Names_Hindi: Gardan se uthne waala sirdard; Cervicogenic Headache
Primary_Symptoms: Unilateral non-throbbing headache originating from neck/occipital region and radiating forward to forehead, temple, or retro-orbital area
Secondary_Symptoms: Neck pain and stiffness; Restricted cervical range of motion; Pain triggered by specific neck movements or sustained posture; Ipsilateral shoulder pain
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Sirdard gardan ke piche se shuru hokar aage aakh ya patti tak jata hai?; 2. Gardan modne ya lambe samay tak jhuk kar baithne par badhta hai?; 3. Gardan me aedan hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Aceclofenac + Physical Therapy
Supportive_Medicines: Thiocolchicoside 4 mg BD (if severe paraspinal muscle spasm present under doctor); Topical NSAID gel; Cervical posture exercises
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs short course (3-5 days) after food. Contraindicated in peptic ulcer, CKD, severe heart failure, uncontrolled HTN, asthma, and 3rd trimester pregnancy. Simple analgesics/topical NSAIDs first-line OTC choices. Muscle relaxants Rx only (drowsiness caution, contraindicated in pregnancy/lactation). Diagnostic/therapeutic cervical facet or greater occipital nerve blocks Rx under specialist
Home_Care_Advice: Maintain ergonomic posture during desk/computer work; Perform gentle cervical isometric exercises and chin tucks; Apply warm compresses to back of neck; Avoid prolonged forward head posture ('text neck')
Lab_Investigations: X-ray Cervical Spine (AP, Lateral, and Flexion-Extension views); MRI Cervical Spine (rule out C2-C3 disc prolapse or spinal cord compression)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Onset of arm weakness, numbness, or loss of hand dexterity; Sudden severe trauma prior to headache; Fever with neck stiffness; Loss of bowel/bladder control

Common_Names_Hindi: Chot ke baad ka sirdard; Post-Concussion Headache
Primary_Symptoms: Persistent headache developing within 7 days following a head injury or concussion, resembling tension-type or migraine headache
Secondary_Symptoms: Dizziness; Fatigue; Concentration difficulties; Irritability; Insomnia; Light and sound sensitivity
Typical_Duration: Weeks to months (usually resolves within 3-6 months)
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Head injury ya girne ke kitne din baad sirdard shuru hua?; 2. Dizziness, thakan, ya dhundla dikhna to nahi hai?; 3. Vomiting ya behoshi hui thi?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Amitriptyline (if chronic persistent post-traumatic headache under doctor)
Supportive_Medicines: Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Rest protocol; Cognitive rest
Precautions_Contraindications: Avoid Aspirin and NSAIDs immediately post-injury until intracranial hemorrhage is ruled out. Never stop or change prescribed psychotropic/neurological medications on your own. Paracetamol is the safer initial choice for mild pain. If headache persists beyond 2 weeks, specialist neurological evaluation is mandatory
Home_Care_Advice: Enforce strict physical and cognitive rest in initial days post-injury; Limit screen time (mobile, TV, computer); Avoid sports, driving, and strenuous physical activity until cleared by a doctor; Maintain adequate hydration
Lab_Investigations: Non-Contrast CT Scan Brain (MANDATORY initially to rule out epidural/subdural hematoma or skull fracture); MRI Brain (if symptoms persist >2-4 weeks)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Emergency Red Flags: Sudden worst headache; Repeated vomiting; Progressive drowsiness or inability to awaken; One-sided arm/leg weakness; Fluid/blood discharge from nose or ears; Seizures; Asymmetric pupils

Common_Names_Hindi: Thunderclap Headache (Emergency); Dimag ki nass phatna
Primary_Symptoms: Sudden, explosive headache that reaches MAXIMUM SEVERE INTENSITY WITHIN 60 SECONDS ('worst headache of life'); High suspicion for ruptured cerebral aneurysm
Secondary_Symptoms: Neck stiffness; Repeated projectile vomiting; Altered mental status; Seizures; Loss of consciousness; Photophobia; Focal neurological deficits
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Sirdard achanak ek minute ke andar life ka sabse severe headache ban gaya?; 2. Ulti, gardan me aedan, ya behoshi aayi hai?; 3. Aankho ke samne dhundla-pan hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: None - emergency hospital referral
Popular_Indian_Brands: Injection Nimodipine IV / Oral Nimodipine (in ICU post-scan)
Dosage_Frequency: Immediate emergency transfer to tertiary neurosurgical ICU
Supportive_Medicines: Immediate ER Transfer; Emergency Non-Contrast CT Brain; Lumbar Puncture (if CT negative); Cerebral Angiography (DSA/CTA); Emergency Neurosurgical / Endovascular Coiling or Clipping
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Life-threatening emergency. DO NOT GIVE ASPIRIN, NSAIDS, OR PAINKILLERS AT HOME (can worsen intracranial bleeding). Do NOT delay seeking emergency transport. Keep patient flat and calm
Home_Care_Advice: Immediate emergency hospital referral to a tertiary care center with neurosurgical facilities; Keep patient lying flat in a dark quiet environment; Do NOT give anything by mouth (NPO) as emergency surgery/procedure may be required
Lab_Investigations: Emergency Non-Contrast CT Brain (within 6 hours of onset); Lumbar Puncture (for xanthochromia if CT is normal); CT Angiogram (CTA) / Digital Subtraction Angiography (DSA)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Emergency Red Flags: Explosive onset worst headache within 60 seconds; Loss of consciousness; Neck stiffness with fever; Pupil dilation; Hemiparesis; Seizures

Primary_Symptoms: Severe new-onset unilateral temporal or occipital headache in patients >50 years, associated with TEMPORAL ARTERY TENDERNESS and JAW CLAUDICATION
Secondary_Symptoms: Jaw pain/cramping while chewing; Scalp tenderness (pain on combing hair); Amaurosis fugax (transient monocular vision loss); Polymyalgia rheumatica symptoms
Typical_Duration: Requires high-dose steroids for months to years
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Umar 50 se zyada hai aur kankhi (temple) me naya severe sirdard hai?; 2. Baal kankhi karne par scalp me dard hota hai ya khana chabate waqt jabde me dard hota hai?; 3. Aakhon ke samne andhera aata hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (High-dose Systemic Corticosteroids - Prednisolone / IV Methylprednisolone under Specialist)
Duration_Days: Rx - specialist supervision required (Months with slow taper)
Supportive_Medicines: Calcium Carbonate 500 mg + Vitamin D3 1000 IU daily; Bisphosphonates (osteoporosis prophylaxis); PPI cover (Pantoprazole 40 mg OD)
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required. HIGH RISK OF PERMANENT BLINDNESS IF STEROID THERAPY IS DELAYED. Steroids must be initiated immediately upon clinical suspicion even before temporal artery biopsy results. Never stop steroids suddenly. Monitor blood glucose, BP, and bone density
Home_Care_Advice: Take oral steroids strictly as prescribed every morning with food; Report any visual changes immediately to doctor; Maintain calcium and vitamin D intake; Do not stop steroids abruptly
Lab_Investigations: ESR (>50 mm/hr, often >100) and CRP (markedly elevated - key diagnostic markers); Temporal Artery Ultrasound / Biopsy (Gold standard); Complete Blood Count
Emergency_Red_Flags: SUDDEN MONOCULAR OR BINOCULAR VISION LOSS / BLINDNESS (OPHTHALMIC EMERGENCY); Double vision (diplopia); Stroke-like symptoms (hemiparesis, dysarthria)

Primary_Symptoms: Progressive daily headache worse in morning and with coughing/straining, blurred vision, transient visual obscurations, and PULSATILE TINNITUS
Secondary_Symptoms: Papilledema on fundoscopy; Diplopia (horizontal 6th nerve palsy); Nausea; Neck stiffness; Associated with obesity or rapid weight gain in young females
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Sirdard ke sath aakhon ke samne achanak kuch seconds ke liye andhera (visual obscuration) aata hai?; 2. Kaan me dil ki dhadkan jaisi aawaaz (pulsatile tinnitus) sunai deti hai?; 3. Aakhon ke doctor ne piche sujan (papilledema) batayi hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (Acetazolamide / Furosemide + Weight Loss)
Supportive_Medicines: Potassium supplements (Syp Potklor SOS as acetazolamide causes hypokalemia); Weight management program; Lumbar puncture (therapeutic)
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required. Acetazolamide is a carbonic anhydrase inhibitor; NEVER STOP OR CHANGE DOSE ON YOUR OWN. Contraindicated in severe renal/hepatic impairment, hyperchloremic acidosis, and sulfa allergy. Requires regular monitoring of serum electrolytes (risk of hypokalemia and metabolic acidosis) and visual fields
Home_Care_Advice: Engage in a structured weight-loss program if overweight (5-10% weight loss significantly reduces intracranial pressure); Avoid Vitamin A supplements, tetracyclines, and oral contraceptives (known triggers); Regular visual field testing
Lab_Investigations: Fundoscopy / Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT - checks papilledema); MRI Brain with MR Venogram (MRV - excludes cerebral venous sinus thrombosis); Lumbar Puncture (opening pressure >25 cm H2O)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Sudden rapid deterioration of vision or peripheral visual field loss (RISK OF PERMANENT BLINDNESS); Severe unremitting headache with persistent vomiting

Primary_Symptoms: Sudden acute unilateral facial weakness or paralysis developing over 24-48 hours, INVOLVING FOREHEAD FROWNING (inability to wrinkle forehead)
Secondary_Symptoms: Inability to close eye; Drooping of mouth corner; Drooling; Hyperacusis (sensitivity to loud sounds); Loss of taste on anterior 2/3 of tongue; Dry eye
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Chehre ke ek taraf ki manspeshiya achanak dhili/paralyzed ho gayi hain?; 2. Aakh poori band nahi ho rahi aur forehead par silvat (wrinkles) nahi ban rahi?; 3. Haath ya pair me kamzori to nahi hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - doctor guidance required (Oral Corticosteroids - Prednisolone started within 72 hours) + Eye Protection
Adult_Strength_Mg: 50 to 60 mg Prednisolone daily total initial
Supportive_Medicines: Lubricating Eye Drops (Carboxymethylcellulose 0.5% q2h); Eye Ointment + Eye Taping at night; Oral Antivirals (Valacyclovir 1g TDS for 7 days under doctor in severe cases)
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - doctor supervision required. Oral steroids must be initiated by a doctor strictly within 72 hours of onset to maximize recovery. Stroke must be ruled out: Bell's palsy involves FOREHEAD wrinkling loss, whereas stroke SPARES forehead and often has limb weakness. Protect affected eye from corneal drying/ulceration
Home_Care_Advice: Apply lubricating eye drops every 2 hours during day; Tape eye closed securely at night after applying eye ointment; Wear protective sunglasses outdoors to shield eye from dust and wind; Perform gentle facial muscle massage and exercises once pain subsides
Lab_Investigations: Clinical evaluation; MRI Brain (if atypical features, recurrent episodes, or no recovery after 6 weeks); HbA1c; Fasting Blood Glucose
Emergency_Red_Flags: Forehead SPARING with lower facial droop AND arm/leg weakness or speech difficulty (STROKE EMERGENCY - call 112); Severe eye pain, redness, or blurred vision (Corneal Ulceration emergency)

Primary_Symptoms: Involuntary, painless, tonic-clonic contractions of muscles on one side of face, starting around orbicularis oculi (eye twitching) and spreading to lower face
Secondary_Symptoms: Involuntary eye closure during spasms; Mouth twitching; Worse with stress, fatigue, or anxiety; Persistent clicking noise in ear
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Chehre ke ek taraf ki aakh aur gaal ke paas achanak apne aap phadkan/khichav hota hai?; 2. Thakan ya stress me badhta hai?; 3. Sirdard ya numbness to nahi hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (Botulinum Toxin Injections / Carbamazepine / Baclofen / Microvascular Decompression Surgery)
Popular_Indian_Brands: Tegretol 100; Lioresal 10; Botulinum Toxin Type A
Supportive_Medicines: Local Botulinum Toxin Type A injections into affected facial muscles (Gold standard treatment, repeated every 3-4 months under neurologist)
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required. Oral medications (Carbamazepine, Baclofen) have limited efficacy and cause drowsiness/dizziness. Never stop prescribed neurological medications abruptly. Botulinum toxin injections must be administered strictly by a trained neurologist
Home_Care_Advice: Manage psychological stress through relaxation techniques; Ensure adequate sleep hygiene; Avoid excessive caffeine intake; Reassure patient regarding benign non-life-threatening nature
Lab_Investigations: MRI Brain with high-resolution CISS/FIESTA sequences (evaluates ectopic neurovascular compression of facial nerve at brainstem exit zone)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Progressive facial weakness or numbness; Hearing loss on affected side; Onset of double vision or balance instability

Primary_Symptoms: Postural and action tremor predominantly affecting both hands/forearms during voluntary movements (holding a cup, writing, using a spoon)
Secondary_Symptoms: Head tremor ('yes-yes' or 'no-no' motion); Voice tremor; Tremor IMPROVES WITH SMALL AMOUNTS OF ALCOHOL and rest; Absence of parkinsonian rigidity or bradykinesia
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Haath me kampan (shaking) tab hota hai jab aap koi kaam karte hain (jaise chai peena, likhna)?; 2. Aaram se haath god me rakhne par kampan ruk jata hai?; 3. Parivar me kisi ko ye problem hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - doctor guidance required (Propranolol OR Primidone)
Supportive_Medicines: Topiramate / Gabapentin (second-line under neurologist); Adaptive heavy-handled eating utensils
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - doctor supervision required. Never stop or change medication doses on your own. Propranolol (beta-blocker) is contraindicated in bronchial asthma, sinus bradycardia, heart block, and uncompensated heart failure. Monitor pulse rate and blood pressure regularly
Home_Care_Advice: Use weighted eating utensils, heavy mugs, and thick pens to damp hand tremors; Avoid caffeine, energy drinks, and stress triggers; Use two hands to hold cups/glasses; Maintain adequate sleep
Lab_Investigations: Thyroid Profile (TSH - rule out hyperthyroidism); Serum Electrolytes; Liver Function Tests; Clinical Neurological Examination
Emergency_Red_Flags: Resting tremor associated with slow movements and shuffling gait (Parkinson's Disease suspicion); Sudden dramatic onset or rapid asymmetric progression

Primary_Symptoms: Asymmetric RESTING TREMOR ('pill-rolling'), BRADYKINESIA (slowness of movement), RIGIDITY ('cogwheel'), and POSTURAL INSTABILITY
Secondary_Symptoms: Shuffling gait with reduced arm swing; Micrographia (small handwriting); Mask-like facial expression; Monotone quiet voice; Constipation; REM sleep behavior disorder
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Haath me kampan tab hota hai jab haath bilkul aaram se god me rakha ho?; 2. Chalne me dheema-pan, pairo ka ghaseatna, ya bina vajah chhote akshar me likhna shuru hua hai?; 3. Balance me kami hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (Levodopa + Carbidopa / Dopamine Agonists - Pramipexole / MAO-B Inhibitors - Rasagiline)
Dosage_Frequency: TDS (Taken strictly 30 mins before meals or 1 hour after meals)
Meal_Timing: Empty Stomach (Protein meals impair Levodopa absorption)
Supportive_Medicines: Trihexyphenidyl 2 mg BD (for prominent tremor in young under specialist); Domperidone 10 mg (for nausea); Stool softeners for constipation
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required. Levodopa/Carbidopa is an antiparkinson drug; NEVER STOP OR CHANGE DOSE ON YOUR OWN (risk of Neuroleptic Malignant-like syndrome / severe hyperpyrexia). Take Levodopa strictly 30-60 mins before protein-containing meals to prevent competitive amino acid absorption blockade. Monitor for levodopa-induced dyskinesias, orthostatic hypotension, and impulse control disorders
Home_Care_Advice: Take Levodopa strictly on time as scheduled by neurologist; Avoid taking levodopa with high-protein meals (milk, paneer, eggs); Maintain daily walking and balance exercises; Install grab bars in bathrooms and remove home tripping hazards
Lab_Investigations: MRI Brain (rule out vascular parkinsonism or progressive supranuclear palsy); Thyroid Profile; Serum Ceruloplasmin (if onset <40 years to rule out Wilson's disease)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Sudden severe fever, extreme muscle rigidity, and confusion following missed levodopa doses (Emergency Hyperpyrexia Syndrome); Frequent unexplained backward falls; Hallucinations

Primary_Symptoms: Recurrent unprovoked seizures (tonic-clonic convulsions, focal impaired awareness, or absence seizures) due to abnormal hypersynchronous neuronal discharge
Secondary_Symptoms: Post-ictal confusion and drowsiness; Tongue biting; Urinary incontinence; Todd's paresis; Aura prior to seizure
Typical_Duration: Chronic condition requiring long-term anti-seizure medication
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Seizures/doure kis tarah ke aate hain (convulsions, behoshi, ya staring spells)?; 2. Abhi kaunsi antiepileptic dawai chal rahi hai?; 3. Dawai ki koi dose miss to nahi hui?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - neurologist supervision required (Levetiracetam / Sodium Valproate / Carbamazepine / Lamotrigine / Phenytoin)
Duration_Days: Rx - neurologist supervision required (Minimum 2-5 years seizure-free)
Supportive_Medicines: Folic Acid 5 mg OD (mandatory for all women of childbearing age); Vitamin D3 supplementation
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - neurologist supervision required. ALL ANTIEPILEPTIC DRUGS REQUIRE STRICT SPECIALIST SUPERVISION. NEVER STOP OR CHANGE THE DOSE ON YOUR OWN; abrupt cessation can precipitate life-threatening Status Epilepticus. SODIUM VALPROATE IS STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED IN PREGNANCY and women of childbearing potential due to high risk of neural tube defects and neurodevelopmental disorders. Carbamazepine requires rash warning (SJS/TEN) and CBC monitoring. Levetiracetam requires monitoring for behavioral/mood changes
Home_Care_Advice: Take anti-seizure medication at the exact same time every day without skipping; Maintain strict sleep schedule (sleep deprivation is a major seizure trigger); Avoid alcohol and recreation drugs; Avoid swimming alone, cooking over open flames, or working at heights
Lab_Investigations: EEG (Electroencephalogram); High-Resolution Epilepsy Protocol MRI Brain; Therapeutic Drug Monitoring (TDM) levels; LFT and Complete Blood Count
Emergency_Red_Flags: Seizure lasting >5 minutes OR multiple seizures without recovering consciousness between attacks (STATUS EPILEPTICUS EMERGENCY - CALL 112); Severe widespread rash with fever (SJS/TEN drug reaction)

Common_Names_Hindi: Mirgi ka daura (First Aid Emergency); Acute Seizure
Primary_Symptoms: Sudden onset tonic-clonic convulsions, loss of consciousness, body stiffening, violent muscle jerking, frothing at mouth, and eye rolling
Secondary_Symptoms: Tongue biting; Urinary or fecal incontinence; Post-ictal deep sleep, confusion, and muscle soreness
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Daura abhi chal raha hai ya khatam ho gaya hai?; 2. Kitni der se seizure chal raha hai?; 3. Kya insan ko hosh aa gaya hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: None - emergency hospital referral (Intranasal Midazolam / Rectal Diazepam in ER or pre-hospital paramedic care)
Dosage_Frequency: Single intranasal dose by trained caregiver if seizure >2-3 mins
Supportive_Medicines: Immediate Emergency Medical Services transfer; Post-ictal recovery positioning; High-flow oxygen in ER
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Life-threatening emergency if prolonged. DO NOT PUT ANYTHING IN THE PERSON'S MOUTH (no spoons, keys, shoes, or fingers - causes airway obstruction or dental fracture). DO NOT RESTRAIN OR HOLD DOWN MOVING LIMBS. Intranasal Midazolam spray Rx under doctor for trained caregivers only
Home_Care_Advice: First Aid Protocol: 1. Lay the person gently on their side (recovery position) to clear airway; 2. Clear the surrounding area of sharp or hard objects; 3. Loosen tight clothing around neck; 4. Place a soft cushion under head; 5. Note the exact time seizure started; 6. Do NOT put anything in mouth; 7. Do NOT restrain them; 8. Call emergency services (112) immediately if seizure lasts >5 minutes, repeats, or person does not wake up
Lab_Investigations: Emergency EEG; Non-Contrast CT / MRI Brain; Blood Glucose (rule out hypoglycemia); Serum Electrolytes & Calcium; ABG
Emergency_Red_Flags: Emergency Red Flags: Seizure lasting >5 minutes (Status Epilepticus); Repeated seizures without regaining consciousness; Seizure in pregnant woman; Difficulty breathing or cyanosis post-seizure; Head injury during fall

Primary_Symptoms: Continuous seizure activity lasting MORE THAN 5 MINUTES, OR 2 or more discrete seizures without complete recovery of consciousness between episodes
Secondary_Symptoms: Persistent tonic-clonic convulsions; Hyperthermia; Cyanosis; Hypoxia; Severe metabolic acidosis; Rhabdomyolysis; Autonomic instability
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Seizure 5 minute se zyada se lagataar chal raha hai?; 2. Bina hosh aaye baar-baar doura aa raha hai?; 3. Patient ER me hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: None - emergency hospital referral
Popular_Indian_Brands: Injection IV Lorazepam / Injection IV Diazepam / Injection IV Levetiracetam / Injection IV Fosphenytoin
Dosage_Frequency: Immediate IV Benzodiazepine bolus followed by IV Antiepileptic load in ER/ICU
Supportive_Medicines: Immediate ER / ICU Admission; Airway management & Intubation; IV Lorazepam 4 mg / IV Midazolam; Continuous IV Levetiracetam or Fosphenytoin infusion; Continuous EEG monitoring
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Critical life-threatening neurological emergency requiring immediate resuscitation. DO NOT DELAY TRANSPORT OR ATTEMPT HOME MEDICATION. High mortality and irreversible brain damage if not terminated within 30 minutes
Home_Care_Advice: Immediate emergency transfer to nearest tertiary hospital ICU via life-support ambulance; Maintain airway clear on side; Do NOT give anything by mouth
Lab_Investigations: Emergency ABG; Blood Glucose; Serum Electrolytes, Calcium, Magnesium; Antiepileptic Drug levels; Continuous Bedside EEG; CT/MRI Brain
Emergency_Red_Flags: Emergency Red Flags: Continuous seizure activity >5 minutes; Respiratory depression or apnea; Hemodynamic collapse; Unresponsive comatose state

Primary_Symptoms: Symmetrical bilateral 'glove-and-stocking' burning pain, numbness, tingling (pins and needles), and sensory loss starting in toes/feet
Secondary_Symptoms: Loss of vibration and position sense; Unsteady gait; Reduced deep tendon reflexes; Allodynia; Dry skin
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Pairo aur haatho me dastaane aur mojho (glove-and-stocking) ki tarah sunn-pan ya burning hai?; 2. Diabetes ke ilawa koi aur bimar (B12 deficiency, alcohol, thyroid) hai?; 3. Samaan chhoot-ta hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Pregabalin OR Gabapentin / Duloxetine + Cause Specific Treatment
Supportive_Medicines: Methylcobalamin 1500 mcg OD; Alpha Lipoic Acid 600 mg OD; Supportive foot care
Max_Safe_Limit_24h: 150 mg Pregabalin / 900 mg Gabapentin / 60 mg Duloxetine
Precautions_Contraindications: Pregabalin, Gabapentin, and Duloxetine are Rx only. Never stop or change prescribed doses on your own; never stop abruptly. Drowsiness, dizziness, sedation, and fall risk caution (especially in elderly). Identify and treat underlying cause (alcohol, toxins, chemotherapy, hypothyroidism, autoimmune disease)
Home_Care_Advice: Inspect feet daily for unnoticed cuts, blisters, or ulcers; Wear cushioned well-fitted shoes and seamless socks; Avoid walking barefoot; Use lukewarm water for bathing (test temperature with elbow to prevent burns)
Lab_Investigations: Nerve Conduction Studies (NCS) and Electromyography (EMG); Fasting Blood Glucose & HbA1c; Serum B12 & Folate; Thyroid Profile (TSH); Serum Protein Electrophoresis; ESR/ANA
Emergency_Red_Flags: Rapidly ascending weakness moving up legs to arms (Guillain-Barré Syndrome suspicion); Sudden onset foot drop; Non-healing infected foot ulcer

Common_Names_Hindi: Vitamin B12 ki kami ka dard; B12 Neuropathy
Primary_Symptoms: Symmetrical paresthesias (tingling/numbness) in feet and hands, sensory ataxia (unsteady walk in dark), loss of vibration/proprioception, and muscle weakness
Secondary_Symptoms: Subacute Combined Degeneration (SCD) of spinal cord symptoms; Glossitis (beefy red painful tongue); Fatigue; Megaloblastic anemia; Memory impairment
Typical_Duration: Weeks to months (reversible with early replacement)
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Pairo me sunn-pan, chiintiya katna, aur chalte waqt balance khona hota hai?; 2. Aap strictly vegetarian/vegan hain?; 3. Vitamin B12 test karwaya hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: DOSE SET BY DOCTOR BASED ON SEVERITY & ROUTE (Methylcobalamin / Cyanocobalamin Parenteral or High-dose Oral)
Dosage_Frequency: OD (Oral) / Weekly IM injection as per doctor regimen
Supportive_Medicines: Folic Acid 5 mg OD; Iron supplementation (if co-existing iron deficiency)
Precautions_Contraindications: Vitamin B12 deficiency treatment dose and route (oral vs intramuscular injection) are set strictly by a doctor based on clinical severity and absorption capacity (e.g., pernicious anemia requires lifelong IM injections). Always check both Vitamin B12 and Serum Folate levels before starting high-dose therapy, as folate alone can correct anemia while masking progressive neurological damage
Home_Care_Advice: Maintain adherence to prescribed oral or injectable B12 replacement regimen; Include B12-fortified foods, dairy products, and eggs in diet (if vegetarian); Avoid excess alcohol; Perform balance and gait training exercises
Lab_Investigations: Serum Vitamin B12 level (<200 pg/mL diagnostic); Serum Folate level; Complete Blood Count (MCV >100 fL macrocytosis); Peripheral Blood Smear; Serum Methylmalonic Acid (MMA) and Homocysteine
Emergency_Red_Flags: Rapidly progressive difficulty walking or frequent falls; Severe spastic weakness in legs; New-onset confusion or dementia

Primary_Symptoms: RAPIDLY ASCENDING SYMMETRICAL FLACCID MUSCLE WEAKNESS starting in lower limbs and moving up to trunk, upper limbs, and facial/bulbar muscles
Secondary_Symptoms: Loss of deep tendon reflexes (areflexia); Paresthesias in hands/feet; Dysphagia; Facial diplegia; Autonomic instability (BP fluctuations, arrhythmias); Respiratory paralysis
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Pairo se shuru hokar kamzori achanak upar haatho aur saans tak badh rahi hai?; 2. 1-3 hafte pehle koi loose motion (Campylobacter) ya bukhar hua tha?; 3. Saans lene me takleef hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: None - emergency hospital referral
Popular_Indian_Brands: Intravenous Immunoglobulin (IVIG - 2 g/kg total dose) / Plasma Exchange (Plasmapheresis) in ICU
Dosage_Frequency: Immediate ICU admission for IVIG or Plasmapheresis
Supportive_Medicines: Immediate ER / ICU Admission; Respiratory monitoring (Forced Vital Capacity - FVC); IVIG 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days OR Plasmapheresis; Mechanical Ventilation if FVC <15 mL/kg
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Life-threatening neuromuscular emergency with high risk of sudden respiratory failure and cardiac arrest. DO NOT DELAY HOSPITAL ADMISSION. Steroids are NOT effective in GBS. Monitor autonomic signs continuously
Home_Care_Advice: Immediate emergency transfer to tertiary care hospital ICU with ventilator support facilities; Keep patient in comfortable supine position; Monitor breathing effort closely
Lab_Investigations: Emergency Forced Vital Capacity (FVC) & Single Breath Count; Nerve Conduction Studies (NCS - shows demyelinating polyneuropathy); Lumbar Puncture (CSF cytoalbuminologic dissociation - high protein with normal WBC count)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Emergency Red Flags: Breathlessness, shallow breathing, or inability to count past 10 in one breath (IMPENDING RESPIRATORY FAILURE); Difficulty swallowing or drooling; Cardiac arrhythmias / extreme BP fluctuations

Primary_Symptoms: FLUCTUATING FATIGABLE MUSCLE WEAKNESS worsened by repetitive activity and IMPROVED BY REST; Fluctuating PTOSIS (drooping eyelids) and DIPLOPIA (double vision)
Secondary_Symptoms: Bulbar weakness (dysphagia, dysarthria, nasal voice); Proximal limb weakness; Chewing fatigue; Respiratory muscle weakness (Myasthenic crisis)
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Aakh ke papote (eyelids) shaam ko ya thakan ke baad neeche girte (droop) hain?; 2. Khana chabate ya bolte waqt achanak aawaaz aur patti dhili hoti hai?; 3. Saans lene me takleef to nahi?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (Pyridostigmine / Prednisolone / Azathioprine / Thymectomy Evaluation)
Dosage_Frequency: TDS or QDS strictly scheduled under Neurologist
Supportive_Medicines: Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Corticosteroid / Immunosuppressant cover; Thymectomy evaluation
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required. Pyridostigmine is an acetylcholinesterase inhibitor; NEVER STOP OR CHANGE THE DOSE ON YOUR OWN. STRICTLY AVOID KNOWN CONTRAINDICATED DRUGS that trigger life-threatening myasthenic crisis (e.g., Aminoglycoside antibiotics, Fluoroquinolones, Macrolides, Beta-blockers, Magnesium, Muscle relaxants). Differentiate Myasthenic Crisis (under-medication) from Cholinergic Crisis (over-medication)
Home_Care_Advice: Take Pyridostigmine strictly 30-45 minutes before meals to facilitate swallowing; Rest frequently between daily tasks; Avoid hot bath soaks and extreme heat exposure; Wear a medical alert bracket
Lab_Investigations: Anti-Acetylcholine Receptor (AChR) Antibodies; Anti-MuSK Antibodies; Repetitive Nerve Stimulation (RNS) test & Single-Fiber EMG; CT Chest (screen for Thymoma)
Emergency_Red_Flags: MYASTHENIC CRISIS (EMERGENCY): Sudden severe breathing difficulty, inability to swallow saliva, severe generalized weakness requiring immediate ICU intubation

Common_Names_Hindi: Thigh ke bahar ka sunn-pan; Meralgia Paresthetica
Primary_Symptoms: Burning pain, tingling, numbness, and heightened sensitivity (allodynia) localized strictly to the ANTEROLATERAL ASPECT OF THIGH
Secondary_Symptoms: No motor weakness; Symptoms worsened by prolonged standing or walking, relieved by sitting; Local tenderness medial to ASIS
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Thigh ke BAHAR aur AAGE ki taraf burning, sunn-pan, ya suiya chubhna hota hai?; 2. Tight belt, tight jeans, ya wazan badhne ke baad shuru hua?; 3. Thigh ki manspeshi me kamzori to nahi hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Pregabalin / Gabapentin + Removal of Compression
Supportive_Medicines: Topical Lidocaine patch / Diclofenac gel; Weight reduction; Local lateral femoral cutaneous nerve block (specialist-administered)
Precautions_Contraindications: Pregabalin/Gabapentin are Rx only; cause drowsiness and dizziness. Simple analgesics/topical NSAIDs first-line OTC choices. Conservative compression release is primary cure. Avoid tight belts, tight clothing, or heavy tool belts around waist
Home_Care_Advice: Loosen tight belts, waistbands, corset supports, and tight jeans; Weight loss if overweight (reduces inguinal ligament compression); Avoid prolonged standing; Apply ice packs to outer hip for 15 mins
Lab_Investigations: Clinical evaluation (Tinel's sign over lateral inguinal ligament); Nerve Conduction Studies of Lateral Femoral Cutaneous Nerve; MRI Pelvis/Lumbar Spine (if femoral neuropathy suspected)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Onset of motor weakness in leg (e.g., inability to extend knee - indicates Femoral Neuropathy, not Meralgia Paresthetica); Persistent bilateral leg weakness

Common_Names_Hindi: Shingles ke baad ka nass ka dard; PHN
Primary_Symptoms: Persistent burning, stabbing, or aching neuropathic pain lasting >3 months in a dermatomal distribution following Herpes Zoster (Shingles) rash healing
Secondary_Symptoms: Severe ALLODYNIA (excruciating pain triggered by light clothing/breeze touching skin); Paresthesias; Itching; Hyperalgesia; Sleep disruption
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Shingles (chhoti matani/phunsiyo waala daad) teek hone ke baad bhi wahan tez burning dard rehta hai?; 2. Kapda choone par bhi tez dard (allodynia) hota hai?; 3. Rash ko kitne mahine hue hain?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Pregabalin OR Gabapentin / Amitriptyline + Topical Capsaicin / Lidocaine
Supportive_Medicines: Methylcobalamin 1500 mcg OD; Topical Lidocaine 5% patch / Gel; Tramadol (short-term SOS under strict doctor guidance)
Max_Safe_Limit_24h: 150 mg Pregabalin / 900 mg Gabapentin / 50 mg Amitriptyline
Precautions_Contraindications: Pregabalin, Gabapentin, and Amitriptyline are Rx only. Never stop or change doses on your own; do not stop abruptly. Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, and fall risk caution (especially in elderly). Amitriptyline contraindicated in recent myocardial infarction, severe heart block, and angle-closure glaucoma. Topical capsaicin should be applied only on fully healed skin with no open lesions
Home_Care_Advice: Wear loose-fitting soft cotton clothing over affected area; Apply topical lidocaine patches or gel to intact healed skin; Protect area from direct cold breeze; Perform gentle distraction techniques
Lab_Investigations: Clinical evaluation; TSH & Renal Function Tests (dose adjustment of pregabalin/gabapentin in renal impairment)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Secondary bacterial skin infection with redness/pus over healed dermatome; Unremitting pain causing severe depression or suicidal thoughts

Common_Names_Hindi: Sar ke piche nass ka dard; Occipital Neuralgia
Primary_Symptoms: Paroxysmal severe shooting, stabbing, or electric-shock pain originating in upper neck and radiating over posterior scalp (occipital region)
Secondary_Symptoms: Scalp tenderness to light touch or hair combing; Pain triggered by neck rotation or resting head on pillow; Unilateral or bilateral occipital point tenderness
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Sar ke piche niche (occipital area) se uthkar upar patti tak bijli ke jhatke jaisa dard jata hai?; 2. Scalp ko choone ya baal banana par tez dard hota hai?; 3. Gardan me khichav hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Pregabalin / Aceclofenac + Warm Compress
Supportive_Medicines: Topical NSAID gel; Muscle relaxant (Thiocolchicoside 4 mg BD if neck spasm present); Greater Occipital Nerve Block (specialist-administered)
Max_Safe_Limit_24h: 3250 mg Paracetamol / 150 mg Pregabalin / 200 mg Aceclofenac
Precautions_Contraindications: Pregabalin is Rx only; drowsiness caution. Oral NSAIDs short course after food. Simple analgesics and topical NSAIDs first-line OTC choices. Greater Occipital Nerve (GON) steroid/anesthetic block Rx and doctor-administered (highly diagnostic and therapeutic)
Home_Care_Advice: Apply warm compresses to back of head and upper neck for 15 mins 3 times daily; Avoid resting head on hard pillows; Maintain ergonomic cervical posture; Avoid sudden forceful neck rotation
Lab_Investigations: Clinical evaluation (tenderness over greater/lesser occipital nerve exit points); MRI Cervical Spine / Brain (rule out C1-C2 lesion or posterior fossa mass)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Onset of focal neurological deficits (swallowing difficulty, arm weakness, ataxia); Fever with neck rigidity; Sudden explosive headache

Primary_Symptoms: Pain caused by a lesion or disease of the somatosensory nervous system, described as BURNING, SHOOTING, ELECTRIC-SHOCK, or STABBING
Secondary_Symptoms: Allodynia (pain from non-painful stimuli); Hyperalgesia; Paresthesias; Numbness; Nighttime pain exacerbation; Sleep disturbance
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Dard kis tarah ka hai (burning, bijli ka jhatka, suiya chubhna, ya sunn-pan)?; 2. Dard kis hisse me hai?; 3. Kitne mahine se dard hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Pregabalin OR Gabapentin / Duloxetine / Amitriptyline
Supportive_Medicines: Methylcobalamin 1500 mcg OD; Topical Lidocaine gel / patch; Physiotherapy
Max_Safe_Limit_24h: 150 mg Pregabalin / 900 mg Gabapentin / 60 mg Duloxetine / 50 mg Amitriptyline
Precautions_Contraindications: Pregabalin, Gabapentin, Duloxetine, and Amitriptyline are Rx only. NEVER STOP OR CHANGE THE DOSE ON YOUR OWN; never stop abruptly (risk of withdrawal symptoms and rebound pain). Drowsiness, dizziness, sedation, dry mouth, and fall risk caution (especially in elderly). Amitriptyline caution in cardiac disease, glaucoma, and urinary retention
Home_Care_Advice: Maintain adequate sleep hygiene; Engage in gentle low-impact physical exercise; Apply warm or cold compresses as tolerated; Use non-drug pain management strategies (mindfulness, relaxation techniques)
Lab_Investigations: Nerve Conduction Studies (NCS) / EMG; Serum B12; Fasting Blood Glucose & HbA1c; Renal & Liver Function Tests
Emergency_Red_Flags: Rapidly progressive muscle weakness or loss of bowel/bladder control; Severe drug hypersensitivity rash; Unremitting agony causing severe depression

Primary_Symptoms: PROGRESSIVE SHORT-TERM MEMORY LOSS, disorientation to time/place, impaired executive function, and difficulty completing familiar tasks
Secondary_Symptoms: Aphasia (word-finding difficulty); Apraxia; Agnosia; Behavioral and Psychological Symptoms of Dementia (BPSD - agitation, wandering, sun-downing, paranoia); Loss of independence
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Purani baatein yaad rehti hain par abhi ki baatein (kya khaya, kahan rakha) turant bhool jate hain?; 2. Raste bhoolna ya ghar ke kaam karne me takleef hai?; 3. Umar kitni hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (Cholinesterase Inhibitors - Donepezil / Rivastigmine / NMDA Receptor Antagonist - Memantine)
Supportive_Medicines: Multivitamins; Behavioral management support; Caregiver stress counseling
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required. Cholinesterase inhibitors (Donepezil) are Rx only; NEVER STOP OR CHANGE DOSE ON YOUR OWN. Donepezil can cause bradycardia, syncope, heart block, gastric ulcers, and insomnia (take at bedtime). Do not expect instant cure; these drugs slow cognitive decline
Home_Care_Advice: Maintain a predictable daily routine; Use memory aids (calendars, clocks, labeled drawers, medication organizers); Ensure home safety (remove tripping hazards, lock gas stoves, secure doors against wandering); Reassure calmly without arguing
Lab_Investigations: MMSE (Mini-Mental State Examination) / MoCA score; MRI Brain (shows hippocampal and temporoparietal atrophy); Serum B12 & TSH (MUST RULE OUT REVERSIBLE CAUSES OF MEMORY LOSS)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Sudden rapid cognitive drop over days (Delirium rule out); Severe agitation, aggression, or hallucinations; Unexplained falls or head injury

Primary_Symptoms: Subjective and objective cognitive decline (memory, language, or executive function) GREATER THAN EXPECTED FOR AGE, but WITHOUT SIGNIFICANT LOSS OF DAILY FUNCTIONAL INDEPENDENCE
Secondary_Symptoms: Mild forgetfulness for appointments/names; Reduced multitasking ability; Normal activities of daily living preserved; Intact self-care
Typical_Duration: Chronic variable condition (may remain stable, revert, or progress to dementia)
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Bhoolna umar ke hisab se thoda zyada lagta hai par daily kaam khud kar lete hain?; 2. Shakk, rasta bhatakna, ya kapde pehenne me koi takleef hai?; 3. B12/Thyroid test hua hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Non-Pharmacological Cognitive Stimulation + Reversible Cause Correction (NO DRUG PROVEN TO CURER MCI)
Supportive_Medicines: Methylcobalamin 1500 mcg OD (if low B12); Thyroid hormone (if hypothyroid); Mediterranean diet; Brain exercises
Precautions_Contraindications: NO PHARMACOLOGICAL DRUG IS APPROVED OR PROVEN TO CURE MILD COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT. Do not prescribe cholinesterase inhibitors (Donepezil) or memory supplements for pure MCI without specialist approval. Correct reversible physical causes (B12 deficiency, hypothyroidism, depression, sleep apnea)
Home_Care_Advice: Engage in regular cognitive stimulation (crosswords, reading, learning new skills, puzzles); Perform 150 mins/week of aerobic exercise; Eat a heart-healthy Mediterranean diet; Maintain active social interactions
Lab_Investigations: MoCA (Montreal Cognitive Assessment); Serum B12 & Folate; Thyroid Profile (TSH); Fasting Blood Glucose; MRI Brain
Emergency_Red_Flags: Rapid cognitive deterioration over weeks; Onset of hallucinations, delusions, or severe personality changes; Motor weakness or gait instability

Common_Names_Hindi: Vascular Dementia; Lakwe ke baad ki bhoolna
Primary_Symptoms: STEPWISE DETEORIATION IN COGNITION following single or recurrent cerebrovascular accidents (strokes/TIAs), with prominent EXECUTIVE DYSFUNCTION and gait disturbance
Secondary_Symptoms: Apathy; Emotional lability (pseudobulbar affect); Focal neurological signs (hemiparesis, exaggerated reflexes); Urinary urgency/incontinence; Slowed thinking
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Sirdard ya stroke/lakwe ke doure ke baad achanak bhoolna aur sochne ki speed kam hui hai?; 2. Har naye stroke ke sath cognition ek step neeche girta hai?; 3. BP/Diabetes/Cholesterol kitna rehta hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (Secondary Stroke Prevention + Donepezil / Memantine under Specialist)
Supportive_Medicines: Aspirin 75 mg OD + Atorvastatin 20 mg OD (Strict secondary stroke prevention); Antihypertensives; Donepezil/Memantine symptomatic under specialist
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required. Primary management is strict control of vascular risk factors (HTN, diabetes, dyslipidemia, smoking) and secondary stroke prevention. Donepezil/Memantine Rx only under specialist. Never stop blood thinners or antihypertensives on your own
Home_Care_Advice: Strictly control blood pressure, blood glucose, and cholesterol; Take antiplatelet/anticoagulant medications without missing doses; Perform physical gait training and fall prevention; Engage in structured daily routine
Lab_Investigations: MRI Brain (shows multiple lacunar infarcts, leukoaraiosis, or strategic territorial stroke); HbA1c; Lipid Profile; Carotid Doppler & Echocardiogram
Emergency_Red_Flags: Acute new stroke symptoms (sudden face droop, arm weakness, speech slurring - CALL 112 IMMEDIATELY); Sudden onset severe confusion or fever

Primary_Symptoms: CLASSIC TRIAD: 1. GAIT ATAXIA ('magnetic' feet glued to floor), 2. DEMENTIA (cognitive slowness/apathy), 3. URINARY INCONTINENCE
Secondary_Symptoms: Frequent falls; Broad-based shuffling walk; Executive cognitive dysfunction; Urinary urgency progressing to frank incontinence
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Classic Triad: 1. Chalte waqt pair zameen se chipakte (magnetic gait) hain?, 2. Bhoolna aur dhimapan hai?, 3. Peshab ka control khoya hai?; 2. Inme se sabse pehle kya shuru hua?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (Ventriculoperitoneal - VP Shunting Surgery Evaluation by Neurosurgeon)
Supportive_Medicines: High-Volume Lumbar Tap Test (Therapeutic/Diagnostic lumbar puncture under specialist); Gait physical therapy post-shunt
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required. NPH IS A SURGICALLY TREATABLE CAUSE OF DEMENTIA. No oral medication cures NPH (Diuretics like Acetazolamide/Furosemide have no long-term efficacy). Prompt neurosurgical evaluation for VP Shunt or Endoscopic Third Ventriculostomy is essential
Home_Care_Advice: Use a walking frame or cane to prevent falls; Maintain clear pathways at home; Keep toilet easily accessible or use adult diapers; Post-shunt surgical wound care and routine neurosurgical follow-up
Lab_Investigations: MRI Brain with CSF Flow Dynamics (shows ventriculomegaly disproportionate to sulcal atrophy - Evans index >0.3); Diagnostic High-Volume CSF Tap Test
Emergency_Red_Flags: Sudden headache, persistent vomiting, drowsiness, or fever post-VP shunt surgery (SHUNT MALFUNCTION OR INFECTION EMERGENCY)

Primary_Symptoms: Transient neurological dysfunction following blunt head trauma, with brief or no loss of consciousness (<30 mins), headache, confusion, and dizziness
Secondary_Symptoms: Amnesia for the event; Nausea; Light/sound sensitivity; Brain fog; Slowed reaction time; Fatigue; Emotional lability
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Chot ke baad behoshi aayi thi? (kitni der); 2. Vomiting, ear/nose se blood/water, ya severe sirdard hai?; 3. Pehle ki baatein yaad hain?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rest Protocol + Paracetamol (FOR MILD PAIN ONLY)
Supportive_Medicines: Cognitive rest; Hydration; Antiemetic (Domperidone 10 mg SOS)
Precautions_Contraindications: STRICT PHYSICAL AND COGNITIVE REST IS MANDATORY. Avoid driving, operating machinery, contact sports, or screen use until cleared by a doctor. DO NOT GIVE ASPIRIN, IBUPROFEN, OR DICLOFENAC immediately post-injury (increases bleeding risk). Apply Canadian CT Head Rule to determine need for emergency CT scan
Home_Care_Advice: Enforce 24-48 hours of strict cognitive rest (no screens, reading, or intense mental work) and physical rest; Return to sports/work gradually step-by-step only after complete symptom resolution and doctor clearance; Have a responsible adult monitor patient for 24 hours post-injury
Lab_Investigations: Clinical Canadian CT Head Rule evaluation; Non-Contrast CT Brain (if red flags present - age >65, >2 vomiting episodes, dangerous mechanism, amnesia >30 mins)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Canadian CT Head Rule Red Flags: Repeated vomiting (>2 times); Sudden worst headache; Progressive drowsiness; Fluid/blood from ears or nose; Seizure; Focal weakness; Asymmetric pupils

Common_Names_Hindi: Head Injury Red Flags (Emergency); Severe Head Trauma
Primary_Symptoms: Severe head trauma with ANY RED FLAG: Loss of consciousness >5 mins, repeated vomiting, worsening headache, focal weakness, or anisocoria
Secondary_Symptoms: Fluid/blood discharge from nose or ears (CSF leak); Post-traumatic seizure; Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) <15; Periorbital ecchymosis ('raccoon eyes'); Confusion
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Chot ke baad behoshi, baar-baar ulti, ya sar me bhayankar dard hai?; 2. Kaan/naak se khoon ya paani nikal raha hai?; 3. Ek taraf ke haath/pair me kamzori hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: None - emergency hospital referral
Popular_Indian_Brands: Injection Mannitol / IV Hypertonic Saline (in ER for raised ICP)
Dosage_Frequency: Immediate emergency transfer to tertiary neurosurgical trauma center
Supportive_Medicines: Immediate ER Trauma Transfer; Cervical spine immobilization; Non-Contrast CT Brain; Emergency Neurosurgical Craniotomy / Evacuation if hematoma present
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Life-threatening surgical emergency. DO NOT GIVE ASPIRIN, NSAIDS, OR PAINKILLERS AT HOME (can trigger massive intracranial hemorrhage). Do NOT move cervical spine if spinal trauma suspected. Keep patient NPO
Home_Care_Advice: Immediate emergency transfer to tertiary neurosurgical trauma center via ambulance; Keep patient cervical spine immobilized using a rigid collar or sandbags; Do NOT give anything by mouth (NPO)
Lab_Investigations: Emergency Non-Contrast CT Brain (Gold standard - checks epidural, subdural, subarachnoid, or intracerebral hemorrhage); Cervical Spine X-ray/CT
Emergency_Red_Flags: Emergency Red Flags: Repeated projectile vomiting; Loss of consciousness; Pupil asymmetry; Fluid/blood from nose/ears; Post-traumatic seizure; One-sided weakness

Primary_Symptoms: CLASSIC TRIAD: 1. HIGH FEVER WITH RIGORS, 2. SEVERE HEADACHE, 3. NECK STIFFNESS (Nuchal rigidity); Rapid onset (<24-48 hours)
Secondary_Symptoms: Photophobia; Altered mental status; Confusion; Petechial/purpuric skin rash (Meningococcemia); Seizures; Kernig's and Brudzinski's signs positive
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Tez bukhar ke sath tez sirdard aur gardan me aedan (stiff neck) hai?; 2. Roshni se takleef, ulti, ya daura aaya hai?; 3. Body par lal-baingani dhabbe (rash) hain?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: None - emergency hospital referral
Popular_Indian_Brands: Injection Ceftriaxone 2g IV + Injection Vancomycin 1g IV + Injection Dexamethasone 10mg IV
Dosage_Frequency: Immediate empiric IV high-dose bactericidal antibiotics + Dexamethasone in ER
Supportive_Medicines: Immediate ER / ICU Admission; Emergency Lumbar Puncture (unless focal deficit/raised ICP present); High-dose empiric IV Antibiotics (Ceftriaxone + Vancomycin + Dexamethasone); Droplet isolation
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Life-threatening infectious emergency with high mortality and risk of permanent brain damage. DO NOT SUGGEST WAITING AT HOME OR ORAL ANTIBIOTICS. High-dose IV antibiotics must be started immediately in ER within 1 hour
Home_Care_Advice: Immediate emergency hospital referral to tertiary ICU; Keep patient in quiet dark room; Do NOT delay transport for any home treatment
Lab_Investigations: Emergency Lumbar Puncture CSF Analysis (high polymorphonuclear pleocytosis, low glucose, high protein, Gram stain, culture, GeneXpert/PCR); Blood Cultures x 2; Non-Contrast CT Brain
Emergency_Red_Flags: Emergency Red Flags: High fever with stiff neck; Non-blanching purpuric skin rash; Progressive confusion or coma; Seizures; Focal neurological deficits

Primary_Symptoms: FEVER WITH ACUTE BEHAVIORAL CHANGES, CONFUSION, ALTERED MENTAL STATUS, or SEIZURES due to viral inflammation of brain parenchyma (e.g., Herpes Simplex - HSV)
Secondary_Symptoms: Focal neurological deficits (aphasia, hemiparesis); Hallucinations; Memory loss; Tremors; Lethargy progressing to coma
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Bukhar ke sath achanak dimagi santulan khona, behoshi, ya ajeeb harkatein (confusion/behavioral change) shuru hui hain?; 2. Seizures aaye hain?; 3. Kitne din se hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: None - emergency hospital referral
Popular_Indian_Brands: Injection Acyclovir 10 mg/kg IV q8h (Empiric anti-HSV therapy in ER)
Dosage_Frequency: Immediate empiric IV Acyclovir initiation in ER
Supportive_Medicines: Immediate ER / ICU Admission; Empiric IV Acyclovir 10 mg/kg 8-hourly; Lumbar Puncture for viral PCR; Continuous EEG; Supportive ICU care
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Critical neurological emergency. Empiric IV Acyclovir must be started immediately in ER for suspected Herpes Simplex Encephalitis to prevent fatal temporal lobe necrosis. DO NOT ATTEMPT HOME CARE OR ORAL MEDICATION
Home_Care_Advice: Immediate emergency transfer to tertiary hospital ICU; Maintain clear airway on side if confused or having seizures; Do NOT give anything by mouth
Lab_Investigations: Emergency CSF Analysis & Viral PCR Panel (HSV-1, HSV-2, Enterovirus, Japanese Encephalitis); MRI Brain (shows temporal lobe hyperintensity in HSV); EEG (periodic lateralized epileptiform discharges - PLEDs)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Emergency Red Flags: Fever with acute confusion or altered behavior; Seizures; Rapidly worsening responsiveness/coma; Focal weakness or speech loss

Primary_Symptoms: TRIAD: 1. PERSISTENT SEVERE HEADACHE, 2. FEVER, 3. FOCAL NEUROLOGICAL DEFICIT (or seizures); Space-occupying lesion in brain parenchyma
Secondary_Symptoms: Nausea and projectile vomiting; Papilledema; Altered sensorium; Neck stiffness; History of otitis media, sinusitis, or congenital heart disease
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Sar me ek hi jagah severe sirdard, bukhar, aur ulti hai?; 2. Haath/pair me kamzori ya daura aaya hai?; 3. Kaan/naak se purana mawaad Aata tha?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: None - emergency hospital referral
Popular_Indian_Brands: Injection Ceftriaxone 2g IV + Injection Metronidazole 500mg IV + Neurosurgical Aspiration
Dosage_Frequency: Immediate emergency IV antibiotics + Neurosurgical Aspiration/Excision
Supportive_Medicines: Immediate ER / ICU Admission; Contrast MRI / CT Brain; Empiric IV Antibiotics (Ceftriaxone + Metronidazole + Vancomycin); Neurosurgical CT-guided stereotactic aspiration or excision
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Life-threatening neurosurgical emergency. Lumbar puncture is CONTRAINDICATED due to high risk of brain herniation from mass effect. Immediate neurosurgical evaluation mandatory
Home_Care_Advice: Immediate emergency hospital referral to a tertiary care neurosurgical center; Keep patient elevated 30 degrees; Do NOT give anything by mouth
Lab_Investigations: Emergency Contrast-Enhanced MRI Brain with DWI (Gold standard - ring-enhancing lesion with restricted diffusion); Contrast CT Brain; Complete Blood Count; ESR/CRP; Blood Cultures
Emergency_Red_Flags: Emergency Red Flags: Severe progressive headache with fever; Sudden onset seizures; Drowsiness progressing to coma; Focal arm/leg paralysis; Asymmetric pupils

Common_Names_Hindi: Neurocysticercosis; Dimaag me keede ki ganth
Primary_Symptoms: Most common cause of acquired epilepsy in developing countries: SEIZURES (focal or generalized) due to Taenia solium encysted larvae in brain
Secondary_Symptoms: Chronic headache; Focal neurological deficits; Signs of increased intracranial pressure (vomiting, papilledema); Hydrocephalus (if intraventricular)
Typical_Duration: Weeks to months (resolves as cyst degenerates)
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Seizures/doure ki dikkat hai?; 2. CT/MRI brain me keede ki ganth (cyst with scolex) batayi hai?; 3. Undercooked pork ya aswachh khana/paani ki history hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - neurologist supervision required (Antiparasitic Therapy - Albendazole / Praziquantel + Corticosteroid Cover)
Meal_Timing: After Food (Fatty meal increases Albendazole absorption)
Supportive_Medicines: Prednisolone 1 mg/kg/day (MUST START CORTICOSTEROIDS 1-2 DAYS BEFORE ALBENDARZOLE TO PREVENT SEVERE BRAIN EDEMA); Anti-seizure drugs (Levetiracetam/Carbamazepine)
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - neurologist supervision required. ANTIPARASITIC THERAPY (ALBENDAZOLE) MUST NEVER BE STARTED WITHOUT PRE-TREATMENT CORTICOSTEROS (PREDNISOLONE) COVERAGE, as parasite dying causes severe inflammatory response leading to brain edema, raised ICP, and status epilepticus. Anti-seizure medication must be continued strictly. Contraindicated during active ocular/spinal cysticercosis (requires surgical removal first)
Home_Care_Advice: Maintain strict hand hygiene and food sanitation (wash raw vegetables thoroughly); Adhere strictly to anti-seizure and steroid medication schedule; Avoid driving or operating machinery until seizure-free for designated period
Lab_Investigations: High-Resolution CT Brain / MRI Brain with contrast (visualizes parenchymal cysts with eccentric scolex, calcifications, or perilesional edema); Fundoscopy (MUST EXCLUDE OCULAR CYSTICERCOSIS BEFORE ALBENDAZOLE)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Status Epilepticus; Severe sudden headache with persistent vomiting (Raised ICP/Hydrocephalus); Sudden vision loss

Specialty_Category: Emergency Medicine / Infectious Diseases / Critical Care
Primary_Symptoms: Severe Plasmodium falciparum malaria presenting with ACUTE HIGH FEVER, SEIZURES, ALTERED CONSCIOUSNESS, CONFUSION, or UNPROVOKED COMA
Secondary_Symptoms: Jaundice; Severe anemia; Hemoglobinuria ('blackwater fever'); Oliguria/Acute kidney injury; Hypoglycemia; ARDS; Metabolic acidosis
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Tez bukhar ke sath patient behosh, confused, ya daure pad rahe hain?; 2. Blood test me Plasmodium falciparum malaria aaya hai?; 3. Peshab ka color kaala/bhoora hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: None - emergency hospital referral
Popular_Indian_Brands: Injection Artesunate IV (2.4 mg/kg at 0, 12, 24h) + Oral ACT post-recovery
Dosage_Frequency: Immediate IV Artesunate bolus in ER/ICU
Supportive_Medicines: Immediate ER / ICU Admission; IV Artesunate 2.4 mg/kg IV at 0, 12, and 24 hours; Frequent blood glucose monitoring; ICU organ support
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Critical life-threatening tropical emergency with rapid progression to multi-organ failure and death. DO NOT ATTEMPT HOME ORAL MALARIA MEDICATIONS. IV Artesunate is mandatory
Home_Care_Advice: Immediate emergency transport to tertiary hospital ICU; Maintain clear airway on side; Monitor blood glucose closely (severe hypoglycemia risk)
Lab_Investigations: Emergency Peripheral Blood Smear (thick and thin films for P. falciparum ring forms and parasite density); Rapid Diagnostic Test (RDT); Blood Glucose; LFT & RFT; ABG
Emergency_Red_Flags: Emergency Red Flags: Unresponsiveness or coma; Repeated seizures; Dark cola-colored urine; Severe breathlessness (ARDS); Oliguria/Anuria

Primary_Symptoms: Subacute onset (1-3 weeks) of PERSISTENT FEVER, INCREASING HEADACHE, NECK STIFFNESS, CONFUSION, and CRANIAL NERVE PALSIES (especially CN III, VI)
Secondary_Symptoms: Vomiting; Lethargy; Hemiparesis; Hydrocephalus; Night sweats; Weight loss; Basilar exudates causing stroke/ischemia
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Purana bukhar, sirdard aur gardan me aedan 1-2 hafte se badh rahi hai?; 2. Aakh ki putli ya chehre me lakwa (cranial nerve palsy) hai?; 3. Patient confused ho raha hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: None - emergency hospital referral
Popular_Indian_Brands: Injection Dexamethasone IV + Anti-Tubercular Therapy (Rifampicin + Isoniazid + Pyrazinamide + Ethambutol)
Dosage_Frequency: Immediate emergency hospital admission for IV Dexamethasone + ATT
Supportive_Medicines: Immediate ER / Hospital Admission; Lumbar Puncture; Empiric ATT (AKT-4) + Adjunctive High-dose Dexamethasone/Prednisolone (tapered over 6-8 weeks); VP Shunt if hydrocephalus
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Critical life-threatening infectious emergency with high risk of permanent neurological deficit or mortality. ADJUNCTIVE CORTICOSTEROIDS (DEXAMETHASONE/PREDNISOLONE) ARE MANDATORY TO REDUCE BASILAR MENINGEAL EXUDATES AND INFARCTS. Never delay treatment while awaiting lab confirmation
Home_Care_Advice: Immediate emergency hospital referral; Ensure complete adherence to 9-12 month anti-tubercular drug regimen once stabilized; Monitor LFTs monthly
Lab_Investigations: Emergency CSF Analysis (marked lymphocytic pleocytosis, very high protein >100-500 mg/dL, very low CSF/serum glucose ratio <0.3, positive GeneXpert/CBNAAT for Mycobacterium tuberculosis); Contrast MRI Brain
Emergency_Red_Flags: Emergency Red Flags: Progressive altered sensorium or coma; Sudden onset hemiparesis (stroke from vasculitis); Hydrocephalus signs (projectile vomiting); Seizures

Primary_Symptoms: Autoimmune CNS demyelinating disease: RECURRENT EPISODES of focal neurological deficits DISSEMINATED IN TIME AND SPACE (e.g., Optic Neuritis, Lhermitte's sign)
Secondary_Symptoms: Optic Neuritis (painful monocular vision loss); Transverse Myelitis (paraparesis, sensory level, neurogenic bladder); Ataxia; Fatigue; Uhthoff's phenomenon (worsening with heat)
Typical_Duration: Chronic condition with relapsing-remitting or progressive course
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Aakh me dard ke sath achanak dikhna kam hua (optic neuritis) ya pairo me kamzori/sunn-pan aaya hai?; 2. Garam paani se nahane par symptoms badhte hain?; 3. MRI brain hua hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (Disease-Modifying Therapies - DMTs: Interferon-beta / Glatiramer / Dimethyl Fumarate / Natalizumab / Ocrelizumab)
Supportive_Medicines: IV Methylprednisolone 1g daily for 3-5 days (for acute relapse treatment under neurologist); Symptomatic medications (Baclofen for spasticity, Gabapentin for neuropathic pain)
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required. ALL DISEASE-MODIFYING THERAPIES REQUIRE STRICT NEUROLOGIST SUPERVISION. Acute relapses are treated with high-dose IV pulse corticosteroids (Solu-Medrol 1g IV daily for 3-5 days). DMTs require monitoring for JC virus (PML risk with Natalizumab), CBC, LFTs, and infections. Do not expect supplements to cure MS
Home_Care_Advice: Avoid exposure to excessive heat, hot baths, and fever (Uhthoff's phenomenon); Maintain regular low-impact exercise and physical therapy; Ensure adequate Vitamin D levels; Pacing daily activities to manage fatigue
Lab_Investigations: MRI Brain and Spine with Contrast (Gold standard - shows periventricular, juxtacortical, and infratentorial demyelinating plaques with 'Dawson's fingers'); CSF Oligoclonal Bands (OCBs)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Acute severe relapse (rapid vision loss, inability to walk, acute urinary retention); Signs of severe infection while on immunosuppressants

Primary_Symptoms: Progressive neurodegenerative disease affecting upper and lower motor neurons: PROGRESSIVE PAINLESS MUSCLE WEAKNESS, ATROPHY, FASCICULATIONS, and SPASTICITY
Secondary_Symptoms: Bulbar onset (dysphagia, dysarthria, tongue fasciculations); Limb onset (foot drop, hand weakness/clumsiness); Emotional lability; Respiratory insufficiency
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Bina dard ke haath, pair ya bolne/ngalne ki manspeshiya lagataar kamzor aur patli (atrophy) ho rahi hain?; 2. Manspeshiyo me phadkan (fasciculations) hoti hai?; 3. Saans me takleef hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (Disease-Modifying Therapy - Riluzole / Edaravone)
Dosage_Frequency: BD strictly 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals
Supportive_Medicines: Non-Invasive Ventilation (NIV / BiPAP for respiratory support); Percutaneous Endoscopic Gastrostomy (PEG for dysphagia); Baclofen (for spasticity); Glycopyrrolate (for sialorrhea)
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required. Riluzole slows disease progression modestly; IT IS NOT A CURATIVE CURE. NEVER STOP OR CHANGE DOSES ON YOUR OWN. Riluzole requires baseline and monthly LFT monitoring for 3 months due to hepatotoxicity risk. Requires early multidisciplinary palliative, respiratory, and nutritional care
Home_Care_Advice: Perform gentle passive joint range-of-motion exercises to prevent contractures; Use thickeners for liquids and modify food textures if swallowing is impaired; Initiate early discussions regarding NIV and PEG tube support
Lab_Investigations: Electromyography (EMG) and Nerve Conduction Studies (NCS - confirms widespread active and chronic denervation across multiple regions); MRI Brain and Spine (rules out structural compressive myelopathy)
Emergency_Red_Flags: ACUTE RESPIRATORY DISTRESS / FAILURE (EMERGENCY); Complete inability to swallow liquids leading to aspiration pneumonia; Severe orthopnea

Primary_Symptoms: TRIAD: 1. ACUTE CONFUSION / ENCEPHALOPATHY, 2. ATAXIA (unsteady broad-based gait), 3. OPHTHALMOPLEGIA (nystagmus, 6th nerve palsy) due to severe THIAMINE (VITAMIN B1) DEFICIENCY
Secondary_Symptoms: Hypothermia; Hypotension; Associated with chronic alcohol dependence, hyperemesis gravidarum, prolonged fasting, or bariatric surgery
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Patient confused, behosh, chalne me ladkhada raha hai, aur aakhon me nystagmus (putli hilna) hai?; 2. Chronic alcohol, severe ulti, ya prolonged starvation ki history hai?; 3. IV Glucose dene ke baad badha?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: None - emergency hospital referral
Popular_Indian_Brands: High-dose Parenteral Intravenous Thiamine (Vitamin B1 200-500 mg IV TDS) BEFORE IV Glucose
Dosage_Frequency: Immediate IV Thiamine administration BEFORE any glucose infusion in ER
Supportive_Medicines: Immediate ER / ICU Admission; IV Thiamine 500 mg IV 8-hourly for 3-5 days; Electrolyte correction (Magnesium cover mandatory as magnesium is a cofactor for thiamine)
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Critical neurological emergency. HIGH RISK OF PERMANENT KORSAKOFF DEMENTIA OR DEATH IF UNTREATED. NEVER ADMINISTER IV GLUCOSE INFUSION BEFORE IV THIAMINE IN SUSPECTED CASES, as glucose loading consumes residual thiamine and precipitates acute fatal Wernicke's crisis
Home_Care_Advice: Immediate emergency transport to hospital ER; Ensure IV Thiamine is administered immediately; Complete alcohol cessation
Lab_Investigations: Emergency Clinical Diagnosis; Serum Thiamine level; Serum Magnesium & Electrolytes; Blood Glucose; MRI Brain (shows bilateral symmetric T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in mammillary bodies, thalamus, and periaqueductal gray)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Emergency Red Flags: Acute confusion with eye movement paralysis; Stupor or coma; Severe hypothermia or hypotension

Common_Names_Hindi: Kaan ki nass ki sujan; Vestibular Neuritis
Primary_Symptoms: SUDDEN SEVERE CONTINUOUS ROTATIONAL VERTIGO lasting days, with horizontal nystagmus, severe nausea, vomiting, and gait unsteadiness, WITHOUT HEARING LOSS
Secondary_Symptoms: Postural instability (leaning toward affected side); Worse with any head movement; Oscillopsia; Spontaneous horizontal-torsional nystagmus suppressed by visual fixation
Typical_Duration: 3 to 7 days (acute phase), gradual recovery over weeks
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Achanak tez ghumar (chakkar) shuru hua jo lagataar chal raha hai?; 2. Nausea, ulti, aur chalne me ladkhadahat hai?; 3. Kaan se sunai dene me kami ya aawaaz (tinnitus) to nahi hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Betahistine + Vestibular Suppressants (Short-term strictly <3 days) + Oral Steroids
Supportive_Medicines: Short course Methylprednisolone / Prednisolone (under ENT/Neurologist); Ondansetron 4 mg TDS (for severe nausea); Vestibular Rehabilitation Therapy (VRT)
Precautions_Contraindications: Vestibular suppressants (Cinnarizine, Dimenhydrinate, Diazepam) MUST BE RESTRICTED STRICTLY TO 3-5 DAYS MAXIMUM during acute phase, as prolonged use inhibits central vestibular compensation and delays long-term recovery. Corticosteroids initiated early by doctor improve vestibular recovery. MUST DIFFERENTIATE FROM CEREBELLAR STROKE using HINTS exam (Head Impulse, Nystagmus, Test of Skew)
Home_Care_Advice: Rest in bed during acute 24-48 hours; Avoid sudden head movements; As soon as acute nausea subsides, begin early active movement and Vestibular Rehabilitation Exercises (Gaze stability and balance training) to accelerate brain compensation
Lab_Investigations: HINTS Clinical Exam (Head Impulse test positive confirms peripheral neuritis); MRI Brain with DWI (MANDATORY IF HINTS EXAM SUGGESTS CENTRAL CAUSE OR STROKE RISK FACTORS PRESENT)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Central HINTS signs (normal head impulse test, direction-changing nystagmus, vertical skew deviation - CEREBELLAR STROKE EMERGENCY); Sudden hearing loss; Focal neurological deficits (dysarthria, facial droop, limb ataxia)

Common_Names_Hindi: Kaan ke andar ki sujan; Labyrinthitis
Primary_Symptoms: Sudden severe continuous rotational vertigo, nausea, vomiting, AND ACUTE UNILATERAL SENSORINEURAL HEARING LOSS or TINNITUS due to inner ear inflammation
Secondary_Symptoms: Gait unsteadiness; Horizontal nystagmus; Ear fullness; Worse with head motion; History of recent viral upper respiratory infection or otitis media
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Chakkar ke sath-sath ek kaan se SUNAI DENA KAM HUA HAI ya kaan me aawaaz (tinnitus) aa rahi hai?; 2. Tez ulti aur ladkhadahat hai?; 3. Hal me koi kaan ka infection ya flu hua tha?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Betahistine OR Cinnarizine + Oral Corticosteroids + Antibiotics (if bacterial otitis media)
Supportive_Medicines: Oral Prednisolone 1 mg/kg/day tapered over 10 days (under ENT specialist); Antiemetics (Ondansetron 4 mg TDS); Vestibular Rehabilitation Exercises
Precautions_Contraindications: Vestibular suppressants short-term only (<3-5 days) to allow central compensation. Oral corticosteroids and antibiotics (if bacterial otitis media) require ENT specialist prescription. Sudden sensorineural hearing loss requires urgent ENT evaluation within 48-72 hours for steroid rescue
Home_Care_Advice: Rest in a quiet room during acute vertigo; Avoid sudden head turning; Once acute phase passes, start vestibular physical therapy; Avoid driving or working at heights until balance recovers completely
Lab_Investigations: Pure Tone Audiometry (PTA - confirms sensorineural hearing loss); MRI Brain & Inner Ear (rules out acoustic neuroma or cerebellar stroke); Tympanometry
Emergency_Red_Flags: Sudden total hearing loss; High fever with severe ear pain, purulent otorrhea, and stiff neck (Meningitis complication risk); Onset of stroke symptoms

Primary_Symptoms: Recurrent episodic vestibular symptoms (vertigo, dizziness, motion sensitivity) in patients with a history of Migraine, lasting minutes to hours/days
Secondary_Symptoms: Migraine headache (may occur during, before, or independently of vertigo); Photophobia; Phonophobia; Visual aura; Motion sickness sensitivity
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Chakkar ke episodes ke sath ya baad me migraine sirdard hota hai?; 2. Roshni, aawaaz, ya gadi me travel karne se chakkar badhta hai?; 3. Purani migraine ki history hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol / Naproxen (Acute) OR Betahistine + Propranolol / Amitriptyline / Topiramate (Prophylaxis under doctor)
Supportive_Medicines: Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Ondansetron 4 mg SOS (for nausea); Flunarizine 5-10 mg OD at bedtime (under neurologist)
Max_Safe_Limit_24h: 3250 mg Paracetamol / 48 mg Betahistine / 160 mg Propranolol
Precautions_Contraindications: Preventive medications (Propranolol, Amitriptyline, Topiramate, Flunarizine) are Rx only under neurologist supervision. Never stop or change preventive doses on your own. Propranolol contraindicated in asthma. Flunarizine contraindicated in Parkinsonism and depression. Avoid overusing acute analgesics
Home_Care_Advice: Maintain strict migraine lifestyle hygiene (regular sleep, hydration, unskipped meals); Avoid known dietary triggers (caffeinated drinks, aged cheese, MSG, alcohol); Perform gentle vestibular rehabilitation exercises
Lab_Investigations: MRI Brain (rule out transient ischemic attacks or posterior fossa lesions); Audiometry and Videonystagmography (VNG - usually normal between attacks)
Emergency_Red_Flags: New-onset persistent neurological deficits (diplopia, dysarthria, limb weakness, facial numbness); Sudden severe unremitting vertigo in older patient with cardiovascular risk factors

Primary_Symptoms: CHRONIC NON-VERTIGINOUS DIZZINESS, UNSTEADINESS, OR FLOATING SENSATION ON MOST DAYS FOR >3 MONTHS, exacerbated by upright posture and complex visual motion
Secondary_Symptoms: Symptoms worsened by walking in crowded spaces (supermarkets, malls), scrolling on screens, or visually busy environments; High anxiety; Absence of active structural vestibular defect
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Mahine me 15 din se zyada floating, swaying, ya room ghoomne jaisa dhimapan rehta hai?; 2. Khade hone, chalne, ya crowded market/screen dekhne par badhta hai?; 3. Pehle koi acute vertigo attack hua tha?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (SSRIs - Sertraline / Escitalopram + Vestibular & Balance Rehabilitation Therapy - VBRT + CBT)
Duration_Days: Rx - specialist supervision required (6 to 12 months)
Supportive_Medicines: Vestibular and Balance Rehabilitation Therapy (VBRT); Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT); Reassurance
Max_Safe_Limit_24h: 50 mg Sertraline initial / 10 mg Escitalopram initial
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required. SSRIs/SNRIs are Rx only. SSRIs take 2-4 weeks to display therapeutic benefit for PPPD; DO NOT STOP MEDICATIONS ABRUPTLY (causes discontinuation syndrome). SSRIs may transiently increase anxiety/dizziness in first 1-2 weeks. Avoid continuous long-term use of vestibular suppressants (Betahistine, Meclizine, Benzodiazepines) as they worsen PPPD
Home_Care_Advice: Actively expose yourself gradually to visually busy environments (do not avoid malls/screens, as avoidance reinforces brain hypersensitivity); Perform daily Vestibular and Balance Rehabilitation Exercises; Practice grounding and relaxation techniques
Lab_Investigations: Videonystagmography (VNG); Audiometry; MRI Brain (MUST RULE OUT STRUCTURAL VESTIBULAR OR BRAINSTEM LESIONS BEFORE DIAGNOSING PPPD); TSH & B12
Emergency_Red_Flags: Sudden acute worsening with focal neurological signs (hemiparesis, ataxia, dysarthria); Recurrent falls causing head trauma; Severe depression with suicidal ideation

Primary_Symptoms: Ill-defined sensation of lightheadedness, wooziness, giddiness, or feeling faint, without a true rotational room-spinning sensation or focal neurological deficit
